correctness.rationale: For arbitrary n>=2, 0<alpha<=1 and deterministic initial opinions, the pathwise centered deviations are (1-alpha)^t times their initial values; conditional independent Bernoulli actions yield h_{t+1}=(1-alpha^2/n)h_t+alpha^2 D0 (1-alpha)^{2t}/n^2. This solves to the displayed finite-time risk. The bounded martingale p_t has binary limit because h_t tends to zero. The martingale terminal-expectation identity gives the exact terminal risk and all covariances. Convexity under fixed sum proves sharp dispersion extrema. The standalone exact-rational finite-state checker ran and passed 80 model instances, 380 finite time slices and 117 dispersion-boundary profiles; finite checks corroborate but do not replace the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The theorem supplies a sharp all-population, all-horizon finite-time error envelope for a recognized stochastic opinion-dynamics model, identifies a strict initial-polarization penalty despite identical eventual success probability, and gives the rank-one covariance geometry. These precise facts quantify a motivated gap between known eventual herding and the finite-time social accuracy and are not an arbitrary parameter census or routine variable substitution. Proof and exact endpoint construction show substantive cross-parameter structure.
